topics.description: The story of Adam — creation, the covenant, the test in Paradise, and his status as first prophet.
topics.name: Adam

topics.description: The story of Nuh (Noah) — his long call to his people, the flood, and salvation on the Ark.
topics.name: Nuh

topics.description: The story of Ibrahim (Abraham) — Khalilullah, the test of sacrifice, and the building of the Ka'bah.
topics.name: Ibrahim

topics.description: The story of Musa (Moses) — the confrontation with Pharaoh, Exodus, and receiving the Torah.
topics.name: Musa

topics.description: The story of Isa (Jesus) — miraculous birth, prophethood, miracles, and elevation by Allah.
topics.name: Isa

topics.description: The story of Yusuf (Joseph) — patience in adversity, betrayal, and rise to authority in Egypt.
topics.name: Yusuf

topics.description: The stories of Dawud (David) and Sulayman (Solomon) — prophets and kings granted unique gifts.
topics.name: Dawud and Sulayman

topics.description: The Quranic narrative of Prophet Lut - his preaching against immorality, hosting of the angelic messengers, and the divine destruction of the people of Sodom. Appears across Surahs 11, 15, 26, 27.
topics.name: Lut

topics.description: The Quranic narrative of Musa's journey with the divinely-guided servant Al-Khidr (Surah 18:60-82), illustrating hidden divine wisdom operating beyond surface appearances.
topics.name: Al-Khidr

topics.description: The Quranic account of the righteous ruler Dhul-Qarnayn who traveled the earth, governed with justice, and built the iron barrier against Gog and Magog (Surah 18:83-98).
topics.name: Dhul-Qarnayn

topics.description: The Quranic narrative of Prophet Zakariyya's supplication for an heir, the miraculous birth of Yahya (John the Baptist), and both prophets' devotion (Surah 19:2-15).
topics.name: Zakariyya and Yahya

topics.description: Quranic stories and mentions of other prophets including Salih, Hud, Shu'ayb, Yunus, Idris, Ayub, and others — each with unique narratives conveying moral and theological lessons.
topics.name: Other Prophets

topics.description: The pivotal migration of the Prophet and companions from Makkah to Madinah, marking a new era.
topics.name: Hijrah to Madinah

topics.description: The military campaigns of the Prophet's era — Badr, Uhud, Khandaq, and others.
topics.name: Battles of the Prophet

topics.description: Fath Makkah — the peaceful liberation of Makkah in the 8th year of Hijrah.
topics.name: Conquest of Makkah

topics.description: The household of the Prophet — referenced in the verse of purification (33:33) and the verse commanding love of the Prophet's close kin (42:23).
topics.name: Ahl al-Bayt

topics.description: The Emigrants and Helpers — praised in the Quran as forerunners in faith, those who gave allegiance under the tree, and models of sacrifice and brotherhood.
topics.name: The Companions (Sahabah)

topics.description: Khuluq Adheem — the Prophet's supreme moral character, described as a living embodiment of the Quran.
topics.name: Prophetic Character

topics.description: Rahmatan lil Aalamin — the Prophet's mercy extending to all creation as his defining characteristic.
topics.name: Prophetic Mercy

topics.description: The Prophet's unparalleled insight, strategic intelligence, and wise guidance in all matters.
topics.name: Prophetic Wisdom

topics.description: The obligatory love and veneration of the Prophet as a pillar of complete faith.
topics.name: Love of the Prophet

topics.description: Nations such as 'Ad, Thamud, and the people of Lut who were annihilated for rejecting their prophets.
topics.name: Destroyed Nations

topics.description: Fir'awn and his court as the archetypal tyrant, whose arrogance led to destruction.
topics.name: Pharaoh and His People

topics.description: Ahl al-Kitab — Jews and Christians referenced in the Quran as previous recipients of revelation.
topics.name: People of the Book

topics.description: Ibar — the moral and theological lessons drawn from Quranic accounts of past nations.
topics.name: Lessons from History

topics.description: Verses in which Allah directly reassures and consoles the Prophet during hardship and rejection.
topics.name: Comforting the Prophet

topics.description: Allah's removal of the weighty burden from the Prophet — a reference to Surah al-Inshirah.
topics.name: Relief of the Prophet's Burden

topics.description: Allah's elevation of the Prophet's name and mention — referenced in Surah al-Inshirah.
topics.name: Elevation of the Prophet's Mention

topics.description: Direct Quranic commands to the Prophet concerning worship, proclamation, and conduct.
topics.name: Instruction to the Prophet

topics.description: Direct Quranic imperatives urging the Prophet toward intensified personal worship and devotion.
topics.name: Devotional Command to the Prophet

topics.description: The Islamic ruling that seeking fundamental religious knowledge is an individual obligation (Fard Ayn).
topics.name: Obligation of Seeking Knowledge

topics.description: Ilm Nafi — knowledge that benefits one in this life and the next, as opposed to harmful or useless learning.
topics.name: Beneficial Knowledge

topics.description: The Islamic principle that knowledge must be accompanied by corresponding practice.
topics.name: Knowledge and Action

topics.description: The elevated status of Islamic scholars and teachers as inheritors of the prophets.
topics.name: Scholars and Teachers

topics.description: Jahl — the dangerous state of lacking religious knowledge, leading to misguidance and sin.
topics.name: Ignorance

topics.description: Hikmah — the capacity to discern truth, make sound judgments, and act in accordance with divine purpose.
topics.name: Wisdom

topics.description: Aql — the human faculty of reason, which Islam affirms as a tool for understanding revelation and creation.
topics.name: Intellect

topics.description: Tafakkur fi al-Khalq — examining the natural world and cosmic phenomena as observable evidence pointing to Allah's existence, power, and wisdom.
topics.name: Reflection on Creation

topics.description: Ghaflah — the dangerous state of inattention and forgetfulness of Allah that leads to spiritual decline.
topics.name: Heedlessness

topics.description: Hidayah — the divine direction that leads the heart to truth, dependent on Allah's grace and human receptivity.
topics.name: Guidance from Allah

topics.description: Dalal — straying from the straight path as a consequence of rejecting truth, following desires, or divine abandonment.
topics.name: Misguidance

topics.description: Sirat al-Mustaqim — the correct, divinely ordained path of Islam that leads to Allah's pleasure and Paradise.
topics.name: The Straight Path

topics.description: The Quranic metaphor of light representing guidance and darkness representing disbelief and misguidance.
topics.name: Light and Darkness

topics.description: Khatm ala al-Qulub — the divine sealing of hearts that persistently reject guidance.
topics.name: Sealing of Hearts

topics.description: Da'wah bil Hikmah — delivering the Islamic message with intelligence, tact, and situational sensitivity.
topics.name: Calling with Wisdom

topics.description: Maw'idhah Hasanah — offering reminders, exhortations, and good counsel to move hearts.
topics.name: Preaching and Admonition

topics.description: Mujadalah — engaging in respectful intellectual discourse to establish truth and address doubts.
topics.name: Dialogue and Debate

topics.description: The prophetically modelled virtue of persevering in dawah despite rejection, mockery, and opposition.
topics.name: Patience in Da'wah

topics.description: Taqlid — uncritical adherence to ancestral tradition without examining its validity against revelation.
topics.name: Blind Following

topics.description: Juhud — stubborn, willful rejection of the truth despite its clarity, driven by pride or interest.
topics.name: Denial of Truth

topics.description: Istihza — ridiculing and making light of Islam, its adherents, or its revelations.
topics.name: Mockery of Religion

topics.description: Lahw — the diversion of attention from truth and faith by amusement, play, and worldly preoccupation.
topics.name: Worldly Distraction

topics.description: The plots, whispers, and strategies of Iblis to misguide humanity and obstruct faith.
topics.name: Satanic Deception

topics.description: Haqq — absolute divine truth as embodied in revelation, the prophetic message, and the nature of reality.
topics.name: Truth

topics.description: Batil — all that is false, vain, or contrary to divine truth, destined to perish.
topics.name: Falsehood

topics.description: The Quranic assurance that Haqq will ultimately overcome and extinguish Batil.
topics.name: Truth Prevails

topics.description: The Quranic account of Allah creating the heavens and earth in six days as the foundation of existence.
topics.name: Creation of the Heavens and Earth

topics.description: The Quranic account of human creation — from clay, then a clot — and the breathing of the spirit into Adam.
topics.name: Creation of Humans

topics.description: The Quranic account of jinn being created from smokeless fire, a separate created kind.
topics.name: Creation of Jinn

topics.description: The Quranic declaration that humans and jinn were created solely to worship Allah.
topics.name: Purpose of Creation

topics.description: The sun, moon, stars, and cosmic order as divine signs for those who reflect.
topics.name: Celestial Signs

topics.description: Allah's provision of rain, rivers, and seas as signs of His sustaining mercy.
topics.name: Water and Rain

topics.description: The earth's stability and mountains as signs of divine engineering for human habitation.
topics.name: Earth and Mountains

topics.description: The diversity of animal life and vegetation as signs of Allah's creative power and provision.
topics.name: Animals and Plants

topics.description: The alternation of day and night as a cosmic sign of divine ordering and human benefit.
topics.name: Day and Night

topics.description: The Quran's description of human development in the womb — from a drop to a clinging clot to a lump of flesh — presented as a sign of Allah's creative power (23:12-14, 22:5).
topics.name: Human Embryology as Divine Sign

topics.description: The Quran's repeated use of ships sailing the sea and winds filling sails as signs of Allah's sustaining power and provision for humanity.
topics.name: Ships and the Sea as Divine Sign

topics.description: Khalifah — the human being's role as Allah's steward and trustee on earth.
topics.name: Vicegerency on Earth

topics.description: The Quranic acknowledgment of human frailty — prone to error, forgetfulness, and haste.
topics.name: Human Weakness

topics.description: Karamah — the inherent honor and dignity bestowed upon human beings by Allah's creative act.
topics.name: Human Dignity

topics.description: The Quranic mention of the passage through childhood, youth, maturity, and old age.
topics.name: Stages of Human Life

topics.description: Ruh and Nafs — the spiritual dimensions of the human being as referenced in revelation.
topics.name: Soul and Spirit

topics.description: Ni'mah — the countless specific and general favors Allah has bestowed upon humanity.
topics.name: Divine Blessings

topics.description: Rizq — all forms of sustenance, livelihood, and provision decreed and delivered by Allah.
topics.name: Provision from Allah

topics.description: The Quranic principle that abundance, wealth, and health are themselves tests of gratitude and proper use.
topics.name: Testing through Blessings

topics.description: Divine tests that come in the form of loss, suffering, poverty, illness, or calamity.
topics.name: Trials through Hardship

topics.description: The less recognized but equally serious test of wealth, health, and ease.
topics.name: Trials through Prosperity

topics.description: Tests directed specifically at one's belief — persecution, pressure to abandon faith, religious adversity.
topics.name: Trials of Faith

topics.description: The Quranic emphasis on prophets enduring the most severe trials as models for believers.
topics.name: Trials of the Prophets

topics.description: Sabr — the prescribed response to external trials, loss, and affliction: enduring without complaint to other than Allah.
topics.name: Patience in Hardship

topics.description: The Quranic directive to seek strength through patience and prayer when facing difficulty.
topics.name: Seeking Help through Prayer

topics.description: Ya's and Qunut — the prohibited state of losing all hope in Allah's mercy, condemned in the Quran.
topics.name: Despair

topics.description: Tamhis — trials as a means of expiation for sins and purification of the soul.
topics.name: Purification through Trials

topics.description: Tamyiz — trials serve to distinguish true, sincere faith from mere outward profession.
topics.name: Distinguishing Believers

topics.description: The way hardship wakes the heedless and returns the straying believer to Allah.
topics.name: Return to Allah through Trials

topics.description: The Quran's use of explicit parables and analogies to illustrate theological and moral truths — verses containing 'their likeness is as...' or 'the example of...'
topics.name: Parables and Similitudes (Mathal)

topics.description: Verses in which Allah poses questions not seeking an answer but to provoke reflection, establish proof, or challenge denial.
topics.name: Rhetorical Questions

topics.description: The isolated, abbreviated letters at the beginning of certain Surahs, whose meaning is known only to Allah.
topics.name: Muqattaat

topics.description: The divine oaths in the Quran sworn by created phenomena to emphasize profound truths.
topics.name: Quranic Oath

topics.description: The only woman named in the Quran — mother of Isa, model of purity and devotion, subject of an entire surah and multiple passages.
topics.name: Maryam (Mary)

topics.description: The wife of Pharaoh who believed in Musa, interceded to spare the infant Musa's life, and is cited as a model for all believers with her prayer for a house in Paradise.
topics.name: Wife of Pharaoh (Asiyah)

topics.description: The unnamed queen in Surah al-Naml whose encounter with Solomon and ultimate submission to Allah is a narrative of sovereignty, wisdom, and guidance.
topics.name: Queen of Sheba (Bilqis)

topics.description: The woman who dedicated her unborn child to Allah's service — her vow, its acceptance, and the birth of Maryam as an answered prayer.
topics.name: Wife of Imran (Mother of Maryam)

topics.description: The Mothers of the Believers — addressed directly in the Quran with specific rulings, obligations, and elevated spiritual status.
topics.name: Wives of the Prophet

topics.description: The Quranic declaration that men and women are equal before Allah in faith, deeds, and reward — no gender distinction in divine accountability.
topics.name: Spiritual Equality of Men and Women

topics.description: The Quranic injunctions on modesty of dress and gaze for both men and women — including lowering the gaze and covering adornments.
topics.name: Modesty and Hijab

topics.description: Quranic provisions protecting women — the obligatory dower, the right to initiate divorce, and prohibition of inheriting women against their will.
topics.name: Women's Financial and Marital Rights

topics.description: The Quranic call to a word of common ground between Muslims and People of the Book — shared monotheism as a basis for dialogue.
topics.name: Common Ground with People of the Book

topics.description: The Quran's theological critique of specific doctrinal errors among People of the Book — the Trinity, claiming Jesus or Ezra as son of God.
topics.name: Critique of Distorted Beliefs

topics.description: The Quranic principle that faith cannot be forced — each person is accountable for their own religious choice.
topics.name: No Compulsion in Religion

topics.description: The Quranic command to deal equitably and kindly with non-Muslims who are not at war with believers.
topics.name: Justice toward Non-Muslims

topics.description: The Quranic prohibition of spreading corruption and destruction on earth — used in verses condemning hypocrites, tyrants, and those who destroy crops and lives.
topics.name: Prohibition of Corruption on Earth

topics.description: The Quranic declaration that animals and birds are communities like humans — affirming their status as created beings with their own relationship to Allah.
topics.name: Animals as Communities

topics.description: The Quranic prohibition of wasting resources and squandering — applied to food, wealth, and the bounties of the earth.
topics.name: Prohibition of Waste and Excess

topics.description: The Prophet's miraculous night journey from Makkah to Jerusalem and his ascension through the heavens — referenced in Surah al-Israa (17:1) and Surah al-Najm (53:13-18).
topics.name: Israa and Mi'raj

topics.description: True prophetic dreams as a form of divine communication — Ibrahim's vision of sacrificing his son, Joseph's dreams, and the Prophet's vision of entering Makkah.
topics.name: Prophetic Dreams

topics.description: The Quranic sanctification of the Sacred Mosque and the Farthest Mosque — as the first houses of worship, direction of prayer, and sites of prophetic history.
topics.name: Sanctity of the Sacred Mosque
